newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - British Energy sees more savings.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - British Energy sees more savings.

text.p: Nuclear power generator British Energy Plc should see further savings from plans to cut 1,460 jobs in the next three years above anuual staff cost savings of 50 million stg, chief executive Robert Hawley told Reuters.
"There will be more...you use less office space, less electricity," he said in an interview on Wednesday.

British Energy said in a statement it planned to cut 1,460 jobs within three years for savings on staff costs of 50 million stg a year with a one-off restructuring charge of 100 million stg, already provided for.
Hawley declined to detail what the extra savings would be.
He said 35 percent of the job cuts would be from support staff in offices with 19 percent from nuclear power stations, giving an overall average of 23 percent staff cuts.
But he said safety would not be jeopardised.
"Safety is our bottom line, not profit," he said.
Hawley said the cuts aimed to make "absolutely sure we are competitive in the market place," adding that there was no plan to close any of the company's eight reactors.
"We want to keep all eight going as much as they can produce and putting it into the market place," he said.
He said dividend policy, laid out in the company's privatisation prospectus, would continue, with payouts covered by cash flow.
Cost cuts should contribute to profits for the company, he said, giving funds to reinvest both in the UK and internationally for growth.
But he declined to be drawn on whether the company might be looking at acquisitions or other forms of investment.
"We are busy looking at all kinds of things," he said.
